purpose: Known defects of the transitional C backend, each with the behaviour it reproduces today, so a fix is noticed and can be promoted. The sixteen defects of issue #27 were fixed in ESP-009.B and now live as regression cases in ../regression/cases.json; the six recorded here were found by the ESP-009.C differential work and reported as issue #39. Each program is valid Core 0.1 that argorixc core-check accepts.

gaps.signature: value block needs an expected scalar type
gaps.note: `loop { .. break; }` used as a statement. spec/core/evaluation.md says `while` and `loop` are statements unless every `break value` of a `loop` agrees, so the statement form needs no value at all. The emitter asks the loop's block for a scalar type anyway.

gaps.signature: value block needs an expected scalar type
gaps.note: `let total: u32 = loop { .. break i * 7u32; };`. The backend documents value breaks as outside the scalar C profile (core_c.rs: "value breaks are not in scalar C profile"), and fails earlier than that message. Recorded so the day the profile grows, the corpus says so.

gaps.signature: this C profile currently matches enum values only
gaps.note: `match` on a `bool`. spec/core/evaluation.md requires `match` to be exhaustive for bool and enum alike, so the bool scrutinee is specified, not an extension.

gaps.signature: constant lowering is not implemented yet
gaps.note: `const LIMIT: u32 = 40u32;` at module level. spec/core/grammar.ebnf has `const_decl` among the items, and spec/core/evaluation.md only forbids executable global initialisers, not constants.

gaps.signature: this C profile currently matches enum values only
gaps.note: `match` on an integer with a literal arm and `_`. The grammar's `pattern` production lists both a literal and `_`, and `_` is what makes a non-enum scrutinee exhaustive. Same message as g19_match_bool, different pattern kind: a fix for one need not cover the other.

gaps.signature: match guards are not implemented in the C profile yet
gaps.note: An arm with `if p0 > 3u32`. spec/core/evaluation.md names guards explicitly ("guards no cuentan para exhaustividad"), so they are part of Core 0.1.
